text: Welcome to this episode of This is My Architecture.
I am Wally from AWS and I'm joined with Matt from Miraculous.
Thanks for having me.
Matt, I'm really excited to hear what Miraculous is doing in a genomic space.
All right, so we are basically a biotech startup based on the Bay Area in San Francisco,
and we are building a platform to make science easy, intuitive, and accessible for everyone.
Cool, and I see you do this with a little bit of IoT.

Yeah, sure.
First of all, it's really important for us on our use case to understand that, as you can see,
we have the device on one side and then we have the users on the other side.
So it's really important to understand that every piece of technology that we have here
is in order to make the user feel closer to the device, especially on workflows that needs user interaction or user feedback.

Yeah.
We are using AWS IoT Core, basically, and we are using the SDK to build a custom software to communicate with IoT Core.
And we are doing this by using TLS connections and the MQTT protocol, which is basically a really good protocol because it uses a small footprint on the network.
And we can have really easily all the messages on the platform.
So you take this molecular data and how do you start ending up visualizing it or even just doing your operations on it?
All right.
So once we have the data on IoT Core, we use the rules engine a lot to route messages depending on the use case.
Like, for example, for visualization and things that are related to commercial thing or business intelligence things,
we send a lot of messages to our Elasticsearch platform.
And from this, we can query them, we can visualize them, and we can feed our commercial team with valuable information.
And then after you have this data and visualization, you also have your internal teams that need access to log information.
So how does that process work?
Yeah, that's correct.
Using the same thing, the rules engine, we can also send data to our CloudWatch.

We can notice the right team and make them understand where is the problem so we can fix it.
And so now to actually get this to your molecular scientist, you have like some internal applications and compute going.

All right.
So, some things that we are performing, we don't need this backend.
So a lot of things are basically route to the lambda and it works like a worker, you know.
We have the information here, we do the processing here, and we send it back to the device a lot of times.
That's the workflow.
And once we have some data that we want to interact with the user, we can send it to the SQS, which is another use case.
And by having the information here, what we can do is decouple the SQS from the ECS.
So we have the device and the ECS decouple.
And it's really great because if we start getting more and more messages on the device, you can scale up really easily, seeing on the amount of messages that are attended or unattended.
So we can grab from that metric and scale up the API.
Great.
